reading.body:
The TierPoint Charlotte Data Center publishes 20,000 square feet of technical space and no IT load figure in megawatts, making its relevance to AI infrastructure scaling impossible to determine from available data.

Certifications alone reveal the facility's role in the data center ecosystem. Six distinct compliance credentials—SOC 1 Type 2, PCI DSS, HIPAA, HITRUST, ISO 27001, and ITAR—qualify it for regulated workloads that hyperscale-only campuses often cannot serve. This is infrastructure for financial systems, healthcare data, and defense-controlled information, not the homogeneous compute farms that drive AI model training. The compliance posture indicates a generalist facility serving multiple industries rather than an AI-focused deployment.

North Carolina shows 19 facilities on this registry with only one publishing a megawatt figure—40 MW. The state's near-total lack of disclosed power data obscures actual capacity. A facility cannot be ranked meaningfully by the absence of information. Without a published power number for this campus, no valid comparison to other sites is possible, and no estimate of its racks, accelerators, or role in grid constraints can be made.
